description: Defines the canonical semantic evaluation rules for TEL expressions. Every well-formed TEL expression (passing TEL-Σ SyntaxCheck) has exactly one structural interpretation under these rules. Ambiguity is a parse failure, not a semantic feature.

evaluation_model.canonical_context: AI Edition module registry, active book invariant set, session context (rtt=1 | coherence=declared | drift=bounded | paradox=structural)
evaluation_model.determinism_guarantee: INV-TEL-002 — every well-formed expression maps to exactly one structural denotation under eval

evaluation_rules.note: Looks up the structural entity declared in the active AI Edition module registry. If not found, evaluation halts with an UnresolvedIdentifier fault — not a default or fallback value.
Numeric, boolean, or string literals evaluate to their own intrinsic values. Booleans ⊤ and ⊥ evaluate to structural truth/falsity tokens.
Resolves to the structural value most recently bound to ID in the current evaluation scope. Unbound reference is a scope fault, not a default.
Structural union: the combined node and relation set of both operands, with relational closure applied. Duplicate nodes merge; duplicate relations are deduplicated.
Relational product: every relation in eval(e1) is applied across every element of eval(e2) within shared constraint scope. Produces a new structural configuration, not a set of pairs.

Directed structural dependency: eval(e1) depends on eval(e2). In the dependency graph, an edge is added from eval(e1) to eval(e2). This is asymmetric — eval(e2) does not depend on eval(e1) under this rule.
Constraint assertion: evaluates e1 and checks it satisfies the constraint denoted by e2. Returns the structural denotation of e1 if satisfied; halts with ConstraintViolation fault if not.
Structural disjointness: returns ⊤ if eval(e1) and eval(e2) share no relational elements; returns ⊥ otherwise. Pure predicate — does not produce a new structural configuration.

evaluation_rules.eval: eval(T[ID]: e1 → e2) = declare_transformation(ID, eval(e1), eval(e2))
evaluation_rules.note: Declares a named transformation in scope. Does not execute the transformation — execution occurs when the transformation is referenced via a symbol_ref in a subsequent expression. INV-TEL-004 is evaluated at application time.
Declares a named constraint in scope. The constraint body eval(e) is stored as a structural predicate. Applied by ⊢ operator in compound expressions.

Evaluates e and checks the result satisfies the invariant identified by ID in the active book's invariants file. If the check fails, the evaluation session is flagged with an InvariantViolation record.

evaluation_fault_taxonomy.label: UnresolvedIdentifier
evaluation_fault_taxonomy.trigger: eval(identifier) where identifier not in module registry
evaluation_fault_taxonomy.action: Halt evaluation. Record fault. Do not substitute a default value.

evaluation_fault_taxonomy.label: ScopeFault
evaluation_fault_taxonomy.trigger: eval(#ID) where ID has not been bound in current scope
evaluation_fault_taxonomy.action: Halt evaluation. Record fault. Do not propagate undefined symbol.

evaluation_fault_taxonomy.label: ConstraintViolation
evaluation_fault_taxonomy.action: Halt evaluation of the ⊢ expression. Record which constraint was violated and by which structural denotation.

evaluation_fault_taxonomy.label: InvariantViolation
evaluation_fault_taxonomy.action: Flag evaluation session. Record violation. Session may continue but all downstream results are marked with InvariantViolation flag.

evaluation_fault_taxonomy.label: TransformationFidelityFault
evaluation_fault_taxonomy.trigger: Application of T[ID] to a valid structure produces an invalid structure
evaluation_fault_taxonomy.action: Halt transformation application. Record EF-005 against the transformation declaration. INV-TEL-004 is violated — the transformation encoding must be revised.

book4_binding.note: TEL semantics for opacity expressions use Book 4 OR operators as structural vocabulary. OR-Ω, OR-Δ, OR-Ρ, OR-Λ, OR-Π are valid identifiers in TEL expressions when Book 4 is in the active module registry.
